_: How a database is written down to be compared after an upgrade. Read by gen_fixtures.py (the expected result, through the Python server's migrations) and by the Rust tests (the result of kb_db::migrations), so both sides ask the database the same questions. Every query returns text or NULL only. 'schema' queries describe the tables; 'tables' lists the tables whose rows are compared; 'columns' lists one table's columns in order; 'cell' is how one value is read.

schema.columns: SELECT m.name, CAST(p.cid AS TEXT), p.name, p.type, CAST(p."notnull" AS TEXT), p.dflt_value, CAST(p.pk AS TEXT) FROM sqlite_master m JOIN pragma_table_info(m.name) p WHERE m.type = 'table' AND m.name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'
schema.indexes: SELECT m.name, il.name, CAST(il."unique" AS TEXT), il.origin, CAST(il.partial AS TEXT), CAST(ii.seqno AS TEXT), ii.name FROM sqlite_master m JOIN pragma_index_list(m.name) il JOIN pragma_index_info(il.name) ii WHERE m.type = 'table' AND m.name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'
schema.index_where: SELECT tbl_name, name, CASE WHEN instr(sql, ' WHERE ') > 0 THEN substr(sql, instr(sql, ' WHERE ') + 7) END FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'index' AND sql IS NOT NULL
schema.foreign_keys: SELECT m.name, f."table", f."from", f."to", f.on_update, f.on_delete FROM sqlite_master m JOIN pragma_foreign_key_list(m.name) f WHERE m.type = 'table' AND m.name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'
schema.virtual_tables: SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE sql LIKE 'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE%'

sqlite.tables: SELECT m.name FROM sqlite_master m WHERE m.type = 'table' AND m.name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master v WHERE v.sql LIKE 'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE%' AND m.name IN (v.name || '_data', v.name || '_idx', v.name || '_content', v.name || '_docsize', v.name || '_config')) ORDER BY m.name
sqlite.columns: SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('{table}') ORDER BY cid

schema.columns: SELECT CAST(table_name AS TEXT), CAST(row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY table_name ORDER BY ordinal_position) AS TEXT), CAST(column_name AS TEXT), CAST(data_type AS TEXT), CAST(character_maximum_length AS TEXT), CAST(is_nullable AS TEXT), CAST(column_default AS TEXT) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
schema.constraints: SELECT CAST(CAST(conrelid AS regclass) AS TEXT), CAST(conname AS TEXT), CAST(contype AS TEXT), pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE connamespace = CAST(current_schema() AS regnamespace)
schema.indexes: SELECT CAST(tablename AS TEXT), CAST(indexname AS TEXT), indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE schemaname = current_schema()

postgresql.tables: SELECT CAST(table_name AS TEXT) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = current_schema() AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE' AND table_name <> 'kanban_change' ORDER BY 1
postgresql.columns: SELECT CAST(column_name AS TEXT) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = current_schema() AND table_name = '{table}' ORDER BY ordinal_position

schema.columns: SELECT CAST(table_name AS CHAR), CAST(ordinal_position AS CHAR), CAST(column_name AS CHAR), CAST(column_type AS CHAR), CAST(is_nullable AS CHAR), CAST(column_default AS CHAR), CAST(extra AS CHAR), CAST(collation_name AS CHAR) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
schema.indexes: SELECT CAST(table_name AS CHAR), CAST(index_name AS CHAR), CAST(non_unique AS CHAR), CAST(seq_in_index AS CHAR), CAST(column_name AS CHAR), CAST(sub_part AS CHAR) FROM information_schema.statistics WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
schema.tables: SELECT CAST(table_name AS CHAR), CAST(engine AS CHAR), CAST(table_collation AS CHAR) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE'

mysql.tables: SELECT CAST(table_name AS CHAR) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE' AND table_name <> 'kanban_change' ORDER BY 1
mysql.columns: SELECT CAST(column_name AS CHAR) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = '{table}' ORDER BY ordinal_position
